title: Interpretable Multi-Graph Deep Learning Framework for Detecting Illicit Blockchain Transactions and Wallets
content:
The anonymity of the blockchain environment provided a solid ground for intricate financial crimes, ranging from money laundering, ransomware payment, and financing terrorism. The current state-of-the-art in fraud detection has several issues, as it does not consider the joint modeling of the evolution of things over time in a sequence of transactions, the underlying complex relationships between transactions and wallets, the ability to provide clear causal justifications for the detected fraud, and the fact that the system collapses when dealing with imbalanced data.
This study addressed all these issues by developing a novel interpretable multi-graph deep learning framework that combines temporal transaction graphs, wallet interaction graphs, cross-graph attention, and path-aware transformer encoders. The system was evaluated on the Elliptic++ dataset, containing 203,769 Bitcoin transactions, 2.23% of them being illicit, 1,268,260 wallets, and 49-time steps. The study compared against the Temporal Graph Attention Network. The results achieved by the study are unprecedented: the transaction-level F1-score was 0.8797, a 5.4% improvement over TGN. The wallet-level F1-score was 0.8454, a 5.6% improvement over TGN. Novel path-level classifier was adopted that achieved a remarkable F1-score of 0.8088, demonstrating that the sequence of transactions carried unique signatures of fraud. 
All results were statistically significant (p < 0.001). The performance degradation, even in the presence of severe class imbalance (positive class ratio 0.01), is 4.25%, a significant improvement over the baseline (9.60-11.62%). The degradation in the presence of 10% labels is 6.65%, compared to 12-15% achieved by the competitors. The path-level explanations are rated as extremely actionable by the experts (4.6/5) with 87% alignment with known fraud patterns, compared to 54% SHAP. The inference time is 3.2 microseconds/node, making the system ready for real-time monitoring. This study conceptually opens the door for multi-level temporal graph modeling in the context of blockchain forensics, introduces the novel paradigm of path-level fraud detection, sets a new state-of-the-art on the Elliptic++ dataset, and represents a significant move towards causal tracing of money movement with interpretable path-level explanations.
